ai.description: This slender sea snake reaches 1.2 meters. It is yellowish-grey with dark, narrow bands and a small head. Distinctive features include a spiny, enlarged scale row on the neck and a compressed tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hydrophis lapemoides* is best distinguished by its unusually large, vertically elongated maxillary teeth and a distinctively narrow, elongated head compared to other sea snakes.
ai.habitat: *Hydrophis lapemoides* inhabits shallow, coastal tropical waters of the Indian subcontinent, typically frequenting sandy or muddy substrates in depths under 30 meters.
ai.behavior: The Arabian Gulf sea snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively foraging for bottom-dwelling gobies and other small reef fish along the seafloor.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis lapemoides* is ovoviviparous, typically producing litters of 2–10 young. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity in the Arabian Gulf.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hydrophis lapemoides* occurs along the western coast of the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the coastal waters of Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Kerala.
